345262.title: Non-uniqueness conjecture for s-deep Zero Linear Recurrence Sequences
345262.statement:
Let $\{G_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be an $s$-deep **Zero Linear Recurrence Sequence** such that $c_{s+1}>s$.

**Non-uniqueness conjecture.** Uniqueness of decomposition is lost for at least one positive integer $N$.

This conjecture concerns when legal decompositions associated with homogeneous linear recurrences fail to be unique. The paper presents it as an empirical conjecture alongside a theorem proving the same conclusion under the additional hypotheses $c_{s+2}>0$ and $c_L>1$; the stated conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

345263.title: Uniqueness conjecture for s-deep Zero Linear Recurrence Sequences with a specified recurrence
345263.statement:
Let $\{G_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be an $s$-deep **Zero Linear Recurrence Sequence** with recurrence relation

$$
G_{n+1}=G_{n-2}+cG_{n-3},
$$

where $c\geq 4$.

**Uniqueness conjecture.** There exists a unique decomposition for each positive integer $N$.

This conjecture addresses the existence of unique legal decompositions in a particular family of $s$-deep Zero Linear Recurrence Sequences. It is presented as an empirical conjecture in the supplied text, with no resolution stated there.

345415.title: Constructive conjecture for uniquely 4-colorable planar graphs
345415.statement:
Let $G$ be a uniquely 4-colorable simple planar graph, meaning that $G$ has exactly one proper 4-coloring up to permutation of the colors. **Constructive conjecture.** Every such graph $G$ arises from a sequence of uniquely 4-colorable planar graphs $G_0,G_1,\ldots,G_k$ where

$$
G_0=K_4,\qquad G_k=G,
$$

and each $G_i$ is formed by taking some embedding of $G_{i-1}$ in the plane, adding a vertex $x$ into some triangular face of $G_{i-1}$, and joining $x$ to the three vertices incident to that triangular face. The source says this conjecture is equivalent to the Fiorini–Wilson–Fisk conjecture, but supplies no information about resolution.

345754.title: The divine coloring conjecture
345754.statement: Let $f$ be a coloring of $\mathbb N$ by the two colors $\{-1,+1\}$. A finite set $A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_n\}$ is **divinely colored** if at least half of $a_2,\dots,a_n$ have a color different from that of $a_1$. **The divine coloring conjecture.** There exists a $2$-coloring of $\mathbb N$ in which every cascade is divinely colored. The problem is a stronger-looking variant of discrepancy coloring and remains open.

346023.title: The inverse-exponent conjecture for multiplier sets
346023.statement:
Let $m$, $n$, and $k$ be positive integers with $m\geq 2$, and suppose

$$
M=\{1,m,m^2,\ldots,m^{n-k-1},m^{i_0},m^{i_1},\ldots,m^{i_{k-1}}\}.
$$

A multiplier set $M$ **splits** an abelian group $G$ if there is a set $S\subseteq G$ such that every nonzero element of $G$ has a unique representation $ms$ with $m\in M$ and $s\in S$, while $0$ has no such representation. **Inverse-exponent conjecture.** If $M$ splits an abelian group $G$ and $|M|=n\geq 2k+1$, then

$$
\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\equiv\{n-k,n-k+1,\ldots,n-1\}\pmod n.
$$

This generalizes the preceding result for $k=1$; the source notes that the conjecture is known for $k\leq 2$, while the general case remains open.

346063.title: Bounds for non-isomorphic maximal Arrow single-peaked domains
346063.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of size $m$. Let $\mathcal{N}(m)$ denote the number of non-isomorphic maximal Arrow single-peaked domains on $A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(m)$ by

$$
\mathcal{P}(3)=1,\qquad \mathcal{P}(m)=2^{m-3}\mathcal{P}(m-1)\quad\text{for }m\geq 4.
$$

**The conjectured bounds.** The number $\mathcal{N}(m)$ satisfies

$$
\frac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathcal{P}(m)+\mathcal{P}(m-1)\bigr)\leq \mathcal{N}(m)\leq \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathcal{P}(m)+2\mathcal{P}(m-1)\bigr).
$$

The conjecture concerns the enumeration of maximal Arrow single-peaked domains up to isomorphism; the preceding discussion motivates it by predicting that domains with inherited permutation $\sigma=id$ comprise at least half of all self-paired domains. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

346267.title: Ziegler's vertex-subset conjecture for duals of simple polytopes
346267.statement: Let $P$ be a simple polytope of dimension at least $3$, and let $P^*$ denote its dual polytope. For a subset $S$ of the vertices of $P$, write $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ for its convex hull. **Ziegler's conjecture.** There exists a subset $S$ of the vertices of $P$ such that $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ has the same combinatorial type as $P^*$. The conjecture is a higher-dimensional analogue of Ziegler's problem for simple $3$-dimensional polytopes. The paper provides counterexamples in every dimension at least $3$, so the conjecture is refuted.

346743.title: Rowmotion-equivariant bijection for minuscule doppelgänger pairs
346743.statement:
Let $(P,Q)$ be a minuscule doppelgänger pair, and let $\mathcal{PP}^{m}(P)$ and $\mathcal{PP}^{m}(Q)$ denote their bounded plane-partition sets. **Minuscule doppelgänger rowmotion conjecture.** There is a bijection

$$
\mathcal{PP}^{m}(P)\longleftrightarrow\mathcal{PP}^{m}(Q)
$$

which commutes with rowmotion.

The case $m=1$ was proved by Dao, using a bijection of Hamaker and collaborators; the conjecture remains open for general $m$.

346765.title: Tightness conjecture for the layer number of evenly distributed point sets
346765.statement:
Let $\alpha>1$ be real and let $d\geq 3$. An **$\alpha$-evenly distributed point set** is a finite point set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying the distribution condition defined in the paper, and $L(X)$ denotes its layer number.

**Tightness conjecture.** There exists an $\alpha$-evenly distributed point set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ such that

$$
L(X)\geq\Omega\left(|X|^{\frac{d+1}{2d}}\right).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the upper bound $L(X)=O\left(|X|^{\frac{d+1}{2d}}\right)$ for higher dimensions is tight. The paper gives a construction establishing tightness in the planar case, but notes that constructing matching examples in dimensions $d\geq3$ is more difficult and suggests vector configurations as a possible approach.

347650.title: The $k$-uniform extremal conjecture for $k\ge4$
347650.statement:
Let $k,b,s$ be positive integers with $k\ge4$, let $n=ks$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$. A **blocking set** is a set meeting every member of $\mathcal F$. Let $\mathcal E(k,n,b)$ be the construction defined in the source. **The $k$-uniform extremal conjecture.** There exists a function $s_0(b)$ such that whenever $s\ge s_0(b)$, if $\mathcal F$ has no perfect matching and no blocking set of size less than $b$, then

$$
|\mathcal F|\le |\mathcal E(k,n,b)|.
$$

This conjecture removes the dependence of the threshold on $k$ from the earlier extremal conjecture and would extend the main result to every $k\ge4$.

349325.title: Grünbaum's Hamiltonicity conjecture for 4-connected maps on the torus
349325.statement:
Let $M$ be a map on the torus, meaning an embedding of a graph in the torus whose faces are disks meeting pairwise only in a vertex or an edge. A map is **4-connected** when its underlying graph remains non-trivially connected after the removal of any three vertices, and it is **Hamiltonian** when its underlying graph contains a cycle passing through every vertex exactly once.

**Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture.** Every 4-connected map on the torus is Hamiltonian.

Hamiltonicity is a central question for graphs embedded on surfaces. The analogous conjecture for 4-connected maps on the projective plane was proved by Thomas and Yu, but the torus statement is presented here as unresolved.

349606.title: Gross–Mansour–Tucker conjecture on orientable ribbon graph partial-dual genus polynomials
349606.statement: A ribbon graph is **orientable** if its underlying surface is orientable, and its partial-dual genus polynomial records the genera of all partial duals. A polynomial is **non-constant** if it has at least one term of positive degree, and it has only one non-zero coefficient if exactly one coefficient in the polynomial is non-zero. **Gross–Mansour–Tucker conjecture.** There is no orientable ribbon graph having a non-constant partial-dual genus polynomial with only one non-zero coefficient. This conjecture concerns the possible shapes of partial-dual genus polynomials of orientable ribbon graphs; the source presents it as an open conjecture following known examples for non-orientable ribbon graphs.

350694.title: Vertex-cut obstruction for betweenness-uniform blow-ups
350694.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ with diameter at least three and having a vertex cut of size one. For graphs $H_1,\dots,H_n$, let $G[H_1,\dots,H_n]$ be the corresponding blow-up of $G$.

**Vertex-cut obstruction.** There are no graphs $H_1,\dots,H_n$ such that $G[H_1,\dots,H_n]$ is betweenness-uniform.

This obstruction identifies a class of graphs that cannot be transformed into betweenness-uniform graphs by the blow-up construction. The supplied text does not provide a resolution status beyond stating the result as a conjecture candidate.

352006.title: Supersaturation conjecture for odd-town families
352006.statement:
Let $[n]$ be an $n$-element ground set, and let $[?]$ be a collection of odd-sized subsets of it. Write $peratorname{op}[?]([?])$ for the number of distinct pairs of sets in $[?]$ having odd-sized intersection.

**Odd-town supersaturation conjecture.** Let $n\geq 1$ and fix $1\leq s\leq n$. If $[?]$ is a collection of odd-sized subsets of an $n$-element set with $|[?]|\geq n+s$, then

$$
\operatorname{op}(\mathcal{A})\geq 3s.
$$

This extends the proved case $s=1$, for which every odd-sized family of size at least $n+1$ has at least three odd-intersection pairs; the conjecture predicts the extremality of the construction obtained by adjoining $s$ triples from vertex-disjoint copies of $K_4^{(3)}$.

352266.title: Exponential graph-size conjecture for alternating-group quotients
352266.statement:
Let $X$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be its automorphism group. Let $A_k$ denote the alternating group on $k$ letters.

**Exponential graph-size conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>1$ such that, if $k\geq3$ and $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ has an epimorphism onto $A_k$, then

$$
n\geq C^k.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by Liebeck's result that $n\geq2^k-k-2$ for $k\geq13$ when $\operatorname{Aut}(X)\cong A_k$, with this bound tight for $k\equiv0$ or $1\pmod4$. The broader quotient formulation is left as a conjecture in the supplied text.

352316.title: The Burning Graph Conjecture for trees
352316.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices. For a set $B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, say that $T$ is **$B$-burnable** if there is a sequence of vertices $X=\{v_1,\ldots,v_j\}$ such that

$$
\bigcup_{i\in\{1,\ldots,j\}}N_{b_i}[v_i]=V(T),
$$

where $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_j\}$. Here $N_r[v]$ denotes the closed radius-$r$ neighborhood of $v$.

**Burning Graph Conjecture.** Every tree $T$ on $n$ vertices is $\{0,\ldots,\lceil\sqrt{n}\rceil-1\}$-burnable.

This is the tree formulation of the general burning conjecture. It remains open in general, while the paper proves reductions for trees of bounded growth and establishes improved approximate bounds.

352535.title: Chen–Liu–Zhang signless Laplacian conjecture for intersecting cliques
352535.statement:
For integers $k\ge 1$ and $r\ge 3$, let $F_{k,r}$ be the forbidden graph from the source, let $S_{n,a}=K_a\vee I_{n-a}$, and let $q(G)$ denote the signless Laplacian spectral radius. **Chen–Liu–Zhang conjecture.** There exists an integer $n_0(k,r)$ such that, if $n\ge n_0(k,r)$ and $G$ is an $F_{k,r}$-free graph on $n$ vertices, then

$$
q(G)\le q(S_{n,k(r-2)}),
$$

with equality if and only if $G=S_{n,k(r-2)}$. The case $r=3$ is identified in the source with a theorem of Zhao, Huang and Guo; the general assertion remains open.

352660.title: Boundary-map dimension conjecture for real Grassmannians
352660.statement:
Let $\delta:H^*(\operatorname{Gr}_d({\mathbb R}^{m-1});Q_n)\to\widetilde H^{*+2^{n+1}-1}(C_d({\mathbb R}^{m});Q_n)$ be the boundary map in $Q_n$-homology, and let $k_n^\delta(d,m)$ denote the dimension of its image. **Boundary-map dimension conjecture.** If $m=2^{n+1}-1+2l$ with $l>0$, then

$$
k_n^\delta(d,m)=\sum_i\binom{2^{n+1}-2}{d-1-2i}\binom{l-1}{i}.
$$

This formula is deduced formally from the preceding conjectural dimension formulas and exactness of the $Q_n$-homology long exact sequence. It remains conjectural because those input formulas are not proved in general.

360151.title: Equality of (3,3)- and (3,4)-spreading numbers on grid graphs
360151.statement:
Let $P_m$ and $P_n$ be paths on $m$ and $n$ vertices, respectively, and let $P_m\square P_n$ denote their Cartesian product. For a graph $G$, write $\sigma_{(p,q)}(G)$ for its $(p,q)$-spreading number. **Spreading-number equality conjecture.** If $m,n\ge 3$, then

$$
\sigma_{(3,3)}(P_m\square P_n)=\sigma_{(3,4)}(P_m\square P_n).
$$

The conjecture concerns the unresolved $(3,q)$-spreading numbers for rectangular grid graphs. Since every vertex of $P_m\square P_n$ has degree at most $4$, the $(3,4)$- and $(3,\infty)$-spreading numbers coincide; the conjectured equality would therefore also identify the $(3,3)$-spreading number with the corresponding bootstrap percolation number, whose exact values are not known in general.

364678.title: Partition rank versus analytic rank conjecture
364678.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $q$ be a prime power, and let $T\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb{F}_q^{n_d}$, with $\operatorname{PR}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(T)$ and $\operatorname{AR}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(T)$ denoting its partition and analytic ranks. **Partition rank vs. analytic rank conjecture.** There exists a constant $C\coloneqq C(d,q)>0$ such that

$$
\operatorname{PR}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(T)\leq C\operatorname{AR}_{\mathbb{F}_q}(T).
$$

This is one of the paper’s three recalled rank-comparison conjectures; the source gives no resolution, while noting that versions with constants depending only on $d$ are the original formulations.
